terms.grammar: preposition with the accusative; also an adverb, “opposite, in return”
evidence: Publil. Sent. R 27: remedium … contrā fulmen
Cic. Att. 13.38.1: cum scrīberem contrā Epicūrēōs
terms.comment: The general word: against a person, a current, a wish (contrā voluntātem).

terms.gloss: against (an opponent); as a defence against
evidence: Sen. Ep. 8.5: domus mūnīmentum sit adversus īnfesta temporis
Tac. Germ. 46.5–6: sēcūrī adversus hominēs, sēcūrī adversus deōs
terms.comment: Literally “turned towards”: so also, of conduct, “towards” someone.

terms.gloss: against (of hostile words, feelings and acts)
evidence: Cic. ND 3.84: ad impietātem in deōs, in hominēs adjūnxit injūriam (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Of words, feelings and acts aimed at someone; the same construction serves for kind ones, “towards”.

phrases.latin: Remedium frūstrā est contrā fulmen quaerere.
phrases.english: It is no use looking for a remedy against lightning.

phrases.latin: ante lūcem cum scrīberem contrā Epicūrēōs, dē eōdem oleō et operā exarāvī nesciō quid ad tē et ante lūcem dedī
phrases.english: before dawn, while I was writing against the Epicureans, I scribbled something to you by the same lamp and with the same effort, and sent it off before daylight

phrases.latin: obsequiō trānantur aquae: nec vincere possīs flūmina, sī contrā, quam rapit unda, natēs
phrases.english: you get across water by giving way to it; you could not beat a river if you swam against the way the current pulls

phrases.latin: cibus famem sēdet, pōtiō sitim exstinguat, vestis arceat frīgus, domus mūnīmentum sit adversus īnfesta temporis
phrases.english: let food still hunger, drink quench thirst, clothes keep out the cold, and a house be a shelter against bad weather

phrases.latin: Menēnius Agrippa plēbem cum patribus in grātiam trāditur redūxisse nōtā illā dē membrīs hūmānīs adversus ventrem discordantibus fābulā
phrases.english: Menenius Agrippa is said to have reconciled the people with the senators by that famous fable of the parts of the body quarrelling against the belly

sources: Lewis & Short: contra · Lewis & Short: adversus · Lewis & Short: in
